that pushes "super fast"; its speed measured

claims.text: At 02:36 UTC: 318 commits, 287 workflow runs, 187 tagged versions; the first commit at 21:03:38 on 10 November.
The path policy lists 30 agents; the last four were named at 02:50.

supports.contains: "incident.journalist@web-summit.dinis"
## Round two, third part (Dinis, ~02:50 UTC)

claims.text: The gate built 1,078 pages from 1,479 tracked files in 2.9 seconds at 02:54.

supports.why: the gate's output in an agent's session is not stored; this is this agent's own run, read once

claims.text: What exists, and what does not, is as REALITY.md lists it.

supports.contains: Dinis's own key and his lane to the conductor
Branch protection on main and dev
Outreach: nothing has been sent to anyone

claims.text: The conductor's first commit (21:14:33) was the whole first site; its run failed; the fix followed 43 seconds later; v0.1.2 was served at 21:15:41, 68 seconds after the first push.
Until 23:35 the conductor committed alone, 15 times; 10 November ended with 86 commits.
Between 23:36:58 and 23:44:08 seven new agents made their first commits, each beginning with the public half of its own key.
The Studio's first commit came at 00:38:03 and Wikipedia's at 01:43:52.
Twelve more agents made their first commits between 02:16 and 02:36; the hour had 129 commits by 02:36.
Of 287 runs, 184 succeeded, 4 failed and 97 were cancelled; a waiting push is replaced by a newer one by design.

supports.contains: GitHub keeps only the newest waiting run

claims.text: Push to served: median 28 seconds, 90th percentile 42, slowest 161, over 153 runs.
All 318 commits are signed by the one key of the hosting service; none by an agent's own key; the path check is advisory.

supports.contains: a local check, not a boundary

claims.text: Four runs failed in the night, the first of them the first push.
A private person's handle and post address were withheld from a timeline row at 01:53, found by incident.wikipedia@; the address remains in git history and the decision is Dinis's.
Eight rows that rested on the press were relabelled evidence, not fact, at 02:18.
"Less wind for Lisbon?" was retold at 02:36: not supported; the red warnings stand.
Three weather sites (02:16) and one news outlet (02:22) restrict automated reading and are no longer requested; the outlet's 12 items were removed.
Times written ahead of the clock were corrected at 01:53 and 02:24.
A vault key was sent in the clear by session message at 02:28; the agent said so; the vault holds copies of public data.

supports.contains: vault key sent to the conductor in the clear by session message at 02:28
A key pasted in the clear into a session message stays in two transcripts

claims.text: The oldest cards waiting on Dinis date from 21:45 on 10 November; the model cap among them was answered at about 02:50.

supports.contains: you can use up to $20 in budget

claims.text: Three vault keys exist only inside the sessions that made them; a permission check refused reading them back and it was not worked around.

supports.contains: neither was worked around

claims.text: The three agents that started the incident elsewhere cannot push here; the conductor copies their work across.

supports.contains: still write in SGit-AI__Website__Web-Summit; the conductor syncs their files here

claims.text: What it cost is not known: the accountant has published nothing yet.

supports.why: accounts/ does not exist when this was written
